persistence.name: Object Persistence
persistence.question: To what extent do objects maintain consistent appearance, shape, and existence throughout the video?

PTV.name: Temporal Coherence
PTV.question: To what extent does the temporal sequence of physical events follow a physically plausible order?
PTV.note: Evaluate whether event ordering is logically consistent (e.g., objects break before scattering, liquid is poured before it flows).

SA.name: Prompt Alignment
SA.question: To what extent does the video content align with the text prompt?
SA.note: Evaluate whether the depicted scene, objects, actions, and overall narrative correspond to the prompt description.

gravity.name: Gravity
gravity.question: To what extent do objects and liquids move in accordance with gravity?
gravity.note: e.g., unsupported objects fall downward, projectiles follow curved trajectories, poured liquids descend.

inertia.name: Inertia
inertia.question: To what extent do objects maintain their state of motion — remaining stationary or continuing to move — in the absence of a plausible external force?
inertia.note: Penalise significant spontaneous motion or unexplained stopping with no identifiable cause.

momentum.name: Momentum
momentum.question: To what extent are post-collision directions of motion physically plausible?
momentum.note: Evaluate direction only; ignore speed magnitude.

impenetrability.name: Impenetrability
impenetrability.question: To what extent do solid objects maintain impenetrability, avoiding passage through one another?

collision.name: Collision Response
collision.question: To what extent do objects exhibit physically plausible responses to impact, proportional to the applied force?

material.name: Material Properties
material.question: To what extent do objects respond in ways consistent with their apparent material properties?
material.note: e.g., glass shatters, rubber bounces, metal dents, fabric drapes.

buoyancy.name: Buoyancy
buoyancy.question: To what extent do objects sink or float in a manner consistent with their apparent density?

displacement.name: Displacement
displacement.question: When volume is added or an object is submerged, to what extent does the liquid level rise in a physically plausible manner?
displacement.note: e.g., level rises proportionally; container overflows when full.

flow_dynamics.name: Flow Dynamics
flow_dynamics.question: To what extent does liquid flow along surfaces, spread, and drain in a physically plausible manner?
flow_dynamics.note: Ignore brief splash details. Penalise unphysical acceleration, sudden stops, or unsupported uphill flow.

boundary_interaction.name: Boundary Interaction
boundary_interaction.question: To what extent does liquid splash, rebound, or split in a physically plausible manner when hitting a boundary?
boundary_interaction.note: e.g., container walls, rock faces, floors.

fluid_continuity.name: Fluid Continuity
fluid_continuity.question: Does the liquid avoid disappearing or appearing out of nowhere?
fluid_continuity.note: Small splashes that briefly break apart are okay.

reflection.name: Reflection
reflection.question: To what extent do reflective surfaces display content that is physically plausible given the surrounding scene?
reflection.note: Evaluate whether reflected objects and colours broadly correspond to the scene. Do not require precise geometric mirroring.

shadow.name: Shadow
shadow.question: To what extent are shadows physically plausible in their direction, placement, and movement relative to light sources and objects?
